appraisal_events.evidence: « Ah ! c'est un si bon homme que le baron, ajoutait-elle, si bien, si dévot, si comme il faut ! Si j'avais une fille à marier et que j'étais du monde riche, je la donnerais au baron les yeux fermés. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Françoise voices sincere, naive admiration for Charlus's respectability and piety, an assessment the reader recognizes as dramatically ironic given the extended preceding portrait of his concealed inversion and controlling conduct toward those around him.

status_effects.explanation: Françoise's household praise adds a local, if heavily ironized, positive appraisal of Charlus's character from within the domestic circle, distinct from the accepted patronage-based elevation of Jupien.

ambiguities: Françoise's effusive praise of Charlus ('si dévot, si comme il faut') is strongly undercut by dramatic irony given the narrator's extended prior characterization of Charlus's hidden inversion and manipulative behavior; it is unclear whether this local praise should carry any real weight or is purely comic naivety, so the status effect is scored conservatively.
